scenario: AITA for joking about my phobia? | I have pretty bad emetophobia (fear of vomit/vomiting) - it's not bad enough to stop me from going outside or anything, but it makes me extremely anxious in situations that I know I couldn't escape if someone throws up, such as on public transit or in a car or something. If someone says they have a stomachache, I will immediately panic and start giving them distance. I can't listen to any graphic vomiting stories at all as they just stress me out and make me feel miserable. I know it's not reasonable, but I've seen therapists about it and I'm trying to make things better. Anyways, yesterday my friend had some sort of stomach bug, and threw up a couple times. She texted the group chat about it, we all wished her well, etc. Today she was at school but still feeling a bit ill. On our walk home, she mentioned to us that she wasn't feeling that well, and we started telling her to stay home the next day if she still felt bad. I made a joke along the lines of, "I'd have to avoid you anyways", because if she got worse tomorrow I really would not be able to be near her without panicking. I realize that the joke was not in the best taste, but she knows about my phobia (I saw a girl vomiting when I was with her, literally sprinted away to get out of the situation, and was shaky for a while afterwards) and figured it wouldn't be that big of a deal. She didn't say anything about it and seemed fine for the rest of the time. Later on I got a text from her that said "why were you worried I'd throw up on you lmao", to which I replied that I have a phobia, which she knows. She said that she would avoid me if she felt worse tomorrow, and then added "not like how I feel matters that much lmao". I immediately felt terrible and apologized - I would never, ever want to make someone feel shitty for this. My behavior can be bad in stressful situations but that doesn't mean I get a free pass to act like a jerk. She hasn't replied and she usually texts back quickly, so I think she's ignoring me. I asked my GF and she doesn't think it was a big deal, but because of my friend's reaction I'm really not sure. AITA?

She texted the group chat about it, and we all wished her well. Today, she was at school but still feeling a bit ill. On our walk home, she mentioned that she wasn't feeling that well, and we started telling her to stay home the next day if she still felt bad. I made a joke along the lines of, "I'd have to avoid you anyway," because if she got worse tomorrow, I really wouldn't be able to be near her without panicking. I realize that the joke wasn't in the best taste, but she knows about my phobia (I saw a girl vomiting when I was with her, literally sprinted away to get out of the situation, and was shaky for a while afterwards) and figured it wouldn't be that big of a deal. She didn't say anything about it and seemed fine for the rest of the time. Later on, I got a text from her that said, "Why were you worried I'd throw up on you, lol." To which I replied that I have a phobia, which she knows. She said that she would avoid me if she felt worse tomorrow and then added, "Not like how I feel matters that much, lol." I immediately felt terrible and apologized. I would never, ever want to make someone feel shitty for this. But then she texted me back, saying, "Why were you worried I'd throw up on you, lol." I replied by telling her about my phobia, which she already knew. She then said she would avoid me if she felt worse and added, "Not like how I feel matters that much, lol." That made me feel terrible, and I apologized. So, the question is, was it wrong for me to make that joke? Did I do the right thing by apologizing, or should I have handled it differently? Let me think about the possible perspectives here. From my perspective, I have a phobia that I'm actively working on. I made a joke in the moment, thinking that since she knew about my phobia, it wouldn't be offensive. But clearly, she took it the wrong way, as indicated by her text message. From her perspective, she might have felt that my joke was dismissive of her feelings or that I was making light of her illness. When she said, "Not like how I feel matters that much, lol," it seems like she felt that I was prioritizing my fear over her well-being. So, was it wrong for me to make that joke? Well, humor can be tricky, especially when it involves sensitive topics like phobias or illnesses. Even though she knew about my phobia, making a joke about avoiding her because of her illness could have come across as insensitive or dismissive. On the other hand, I did apologize immediately when I realized she was upset, which shows that I care about her feelings and want to make things right. Apologizing is an important step in repairing the relationship. But maybe I should have handled the situation differently from the start. Instead of making a joke, I could have communicated my feelings more clearly and respectfully. For example, I could have said something like, "I'm really worried about your health, but I have a fear of vomiting, so I might need to keep some distance if you're not feeling well." That way, I'm being honest about my feelings without making a joke that could be misinterpreted. Another thing to consider is how my phobia affects my interactions with others. While it's important to manage my fears, it's also crucial to be considerate of others' feelings and not let my fears dictate how I treat them.
